blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Mask the domain too (or replace the address with a keyed hash or opaque user id); a personal or small-company domain plus an initial still identifies the person, so the logs keep personal data for 90 days (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation).
findings.title: Masked address keeps the full domain and first letter

findings.recommendation: Also mask URL-encoded addresses (`ada%40example.org`, common in logged URLs and query strings), internationalised domains, and local parts with RFC 5322 characters such as `'` (`o'brien@example.com` becomes `o'b***@example.com`, leaking the prefix); add a test per case. GDPR Art. 5(1)(f), Art. 25.
findings.title: Addresses the pattern misses still reach the logs in full or in part

findings.recommendation: Mask the keys as well (`safe[maskEmails(key)]`), since a caller building fields keyed by address (e.g. `{ [user.email]: attempts }`) would log the address in full.
findings.title: Field keys are written unmasked

findings.recommendation: Add a test on `logInfo` capturing `console.log` and checking that an address in `message` and in a string field never appears in full — the guarantee the proposal promises ("masks every e-mail address in the message and the fields").
findings.title: No test proves that log fields are masked

findings.evidence: Our logs are kept 90 days by the hosting provider and contain customers' e-mail addresses.
findings.recommendation: Decide with the team whether existing logs at the hosting provider (a processor, GDPR Art. 28) must be purged or left to expire, and state it in the change; the masking only protects future lines (Art. 5(1)(e)).
findings.title: Logs already written keep full addresses for 90 days
